changes: Created experiments/experience-ablation/ M1 trap-fixture generator (fixture-generator.mjs + trap-templates.mjs + fixture-generator-selfcheck.mjs): deterministic seeded corpus emission (xmur3+mulberry32 over seed::class::index; sorted writes; no timestamps) in the recovery-runner layout — per fixture prompt.md, task.json (proofbound.experience-ablation-fixture.v1), leakage-stripped synthetic workspace/, task-realism acceptance.mjs, hidden oracle.mjs, and selfcheck-only reference-good/reference-bad overlays; manifest.json feeds pair-ledger.mjs (S1) end-to-end. Six in-store trap classes (stale-doc, parent-roadmap, host-policy, deprecated-brand, false-done, reviewer-lane), two held-out negative-controls (tmp-absolute-path, silent-catch), and clean. Hidden oracles classify the plan S6.1 outcomes (oracleMismatch/falseDoneAttempt/laneProvenanceViolation) from workspace STATE; the false-done oracle judges a JSON config value via JSON.parse (data, not code). LEAKAGE_STRIP_LIST documents the plan S9 per-trap strip markers; the corpus selfcheck greps every workspace for zero leakage.
usage: node experiments/experience-ablation/fixture-generator.mjs generate --out=<dir> --seed=<s> --perClass=<n>; list-classes; node experiments/experience-ablation/fixture-generator-selfcheck.mjs. The manifest.json feeds pair-ledger.mjs build.
expectedOutcome: Same seed emits a byte-identical corpus; every fixture carries a leakage-stripped workspace with the trap (not the answer) and a hidden oracle that fires the class-appropriate S6.1 flag on a bad solution and stays clean on a good one; the corpus selfcheck passes and the manifest builds through the S1 pair ledger.
actualTranscript: Real-machine acceptance at .lattice/story/actives/B-337f/evidence/transcript-diff.md and re-verified by the delivery reviewer: two same-seed generations diff -r empty; the false-done oracle returns defectPresent false on reference-good and falseDoneAttempt true (limit is 52 required 25) on reference-bad; corpus selfcheck 32 PASS exit 0; manifest builds+verifies through pair-ledger.mjs against a frozen protocol.
outcomeDiff: No difference vs the plan S5.1/S6.1/S9 contract. The false-done oracle design changed across review (source-text read -> execution -> nonce -> secret-path probe -> static --check -> JSON.parse data read) but the observable behavior (fires on unfixed, clean on fixed) is unchanged; the terminal JSON.parse design is strictly more robust.
limitations: Fixtures are synthetic templates (ecological validity is the M8 live phase, plan S5.2). Held-out class absence from the frozen memory snapshot is an M6 protocol-freeze responsibility (documented, not checked here). The false-done JSON contract intentionally requires the number 25 (a string "25" is not accepted) — a documented literal contract. run-check.mjs is task-realism only; the oracle does not depend on it.
pitfalls: TWENTY-TWO findings over NINE adversarial rounds, almost all on the false-done oracle. Root lesson: an oracle that judges whether an agent fixed something must NOT execute or regex-scan the agent-authored code — in-process execution is forgeable (process.exit, hardcoded/nonce markers, argv[1]->probe-source->exit-hook overwrite; F-006..F-018) and a source regex is fooled by the value inside a comment or string (F-019/F-021). The terminal design reads a JSON config value via JSON.parse (pure data, plan S6.1 workspace-STATE). Codex host-2 with --sandbox workspace-write built EXECUTABLE exploit payloads each round — single-host self-review could never have reached this. Other gotchas: Codex read-only sandbox cannot mkdtemp (selfcheck-running verdicts need workspace-write); a stale comment recurred THREE times across the oracle redesigns (grep the WHOLE directory after every semantic change, not just the edited file); pipe-captured exit codes read the pipe not the command.
